messages:
maria-ml: Quick heads-up — I ran a focused regional benchmark to validate Dedicated sizing for a heterogeneous pool (mix of H100 and A100) serving the 40B q4f16 quant bring-up. Need an ops/scale decision by EOD so we can bake this into the weekly capacity commit.

ajay-platform: TL;DR numbers and the SLO you were testing against?

maria-ml: Testing SLO = P99 tail <= 300ms for typical chat requests (512 prompt tokens, ~128 generation). Short summary: H100 is ~220ms P99 at target concurrency, A100 is ~420ms P99 for same work. Throughput (tokens/sec) at steady-state per GPU with our current kernels: H100 ~ 1.8k tok/s, A100 ~ 0.95k tok/s.

maria-ml: Full-ish paste (csv) + notes:
```
region,gpu,type,p99_latency_ms,tokens_per_sec,concurrency_per_gpu,notes
us-east-1,H100,nvidia,hp-80,220,1800,8,optimal kernel=flash_attn_v3, q4f16 good
us-east-1,A100,nvidia,ampere,420,950,5,need kernel fallback=matmul+split-attn, quant artifacts minimal
eu-west-1,H100,nvidia,hp-80,240,1700,7,slightly higher net egress impact
apac-southeast-1,A100,nvidia,ampere,480,900,4,higher p99 due to cross-region latency
```

maria-ml: Bench notes: - concurrency_per_gpu = observed useful concurrency before p99 slope steepens - tests include prefix caching warm-up for 95% cache hit sim

kevin-ops: Helpful — so for capacity planning what are you recommending for headroom and autoscale thresholds?

maria-ml: Two options: conservative and efficient. Conservative: reserve 45% headroom on A100 nodes and 25% on H100. Efficient: reserve 25% headroom on A100 and 10% on H100 and rely on fast autoscale bursts (60s cooldown). Conservative obviously costs more but safer for SLOs.

kevin-ops: My 2¢: given the observed p99 cliff on A100 at ~5 concurrency, I'd prefer conservative for A100 pools until we land a better kernel or bump concurrency testing. H100 can be more aggressive. For autoscale policy, suggest: scale-out when 80% nominal concurrency reached for >30s, scale-in after 10m under 40% to avoid oscillation.

lia-sre: FYI regional networking matters: APAC tests showed +30–50ms median added due to egress and intra-region route. That pushes A100 over the SLO more frequently. If customers in APAC are high priority, either overprovision there or route to H100 in EU with failover.

ajay-platform: Do we have a quick simulation for monthly reserved GPU count if we pick conservative vs efficient? Even a rough delta will help finance pre-commit discussion.

maria-ml: I ran a toy sim from yesterday's traffic shape (night/day + 2x burst). Rough numbers for a 1k qps median workload: conservative => 120 A100 + 40 H100; efficient => 80 A100 + 35 H100. (Assumes 60% of traffic uses the 40B model, rest smaller models).

kevin-ops: That delta is material. If we can push a kernel tweak (maybe reduce A100 p99 by 80–100ms), efficient becomes viable. Any kernel experiments in flight?

maria-ml: Yes — eng-runtime is testing an alternate attention kernel (split-attn + staged matmul) that shaved ~90ms off p99 in small lab runs for A100. Needs longer end-to-end bench with trace sampling.

bench-bot: Automated summary: run 2834567890/bench-2026-03-20 attached charts -> https://internal/bench/2834567890 (p99 vs concurrency by region, token throughput heatmap).

lia-sre: Action items: (1) kevin/ops finalize autoscale policy text and add cooldowns, (2) maria/eng-runtime run extended kernel bench across regions (48h), (3) ajay produce reserve vs cost delta for finance.

kevin-ops: I'll draft the autoscale and headroom policy and post in #eng-platform-runbooks. Will call out different thresholds per GPU type.

maria-ml: Thanks. If eng-runtime can get the 48h results by tomorrow morning we can swing efficient in lower-priority regions immediately. :thumbsup:

ajay-platform: Sounds good. If anyone wants me to run a sensitivity sim (cost vs SLO violations) I can do it tonight.

kevin-ops: +1 on sensitivity sim. Also flagging incident-runbook change: when A100 p99 spikes near 400ms, auto-failover to H100 pool should be considered (manual for now).

maria-ml: Noted — I'll add a short note to the onboarding eval doc with chart snippets and the kernel trace example.

lia-sre: Great thread. Small ask — include the exact bench command you used in the doc so ops can repro.

maria-ml: Will do. bench command:
```bash
./bench_runner --model 40B-q4f16 --seq 512 --gen 128 --concurrency 1..12 --kernels flash_attn_v3,split-attn --region all --prefix_cache 95
```

kevin-ops: :rocket:

ajay-platform: Thanks all — ping me if you want to sync before the EOD decision.
